Overview

Sarajevo as a Business Centre

Sarajevo is the political and economic centre of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It hosts the state institutions, the parliament and government of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the government of Sarajevo Canton, embassies and international organisations. The canton had 413,593 residents at the 2013 census, and the city and canton are estimated to generate more than a third of national output. The Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina, many commercial banks and the Sarajevo securities exchange are based here. The economy combines services, trade, telecommunications and public administration with manufacturing in food and beverages, furniture, pharmaceuticals, metalworking and vehicle assembly, and a tourism sector that has grown with visitors from Europe, Turkey and the Gulf.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Sarajevo because the city is where foreign investment, privatisation and public money in the Federation are decided. Investors and lenders need to understand the owners and political connections of local partners, since beneficial ownership is not publicly registered. Real estate and tourism projects funded from abroad raise questions about land title, permits and counterparties. Public procurement, state-owned enterprises and donor-funded projects attract integrity concerns. Companies doing business across the Federation, Republika Srpska and Brčko District face fragmented registers and rules. Litigators and creditors need witness, asset and corporate history research for proceedings before the courts sitting in Sarajevo.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Sarajevo

01

Partner and investor due diligence

Foreign investors entering Bosnia often do so through Sarajevo partners. With no public beneficial ownership register, we research registered founders, directors, related companies, court cases, media coverage and political exposure to give a sourced picture of who stands behind a counterparty before investment or contracting.

02

Real estate and tourism projects

Sarajevo has drawn foreign-funded residential and tourism developments. We research developers, landholding companies and principals, and with local counsel review what land, cadastre and permit records show, so buyers and financiers understand title risk, disputes and counterparty history before committing.

03

Procurement and state enterprise integrity

Contracts from state, Federation and cantonal bodies and public enterprises in Sarajevo carry integrity risk. We map relationships between bidders, subcontractors and politically exposed persons from registers, procurement notices and media, for bidders, lenders, donors and counsel assessing a contract or allegation.

04

Cross-entity corporate research

Groups based in Sarajevo often hold companies in Republika Srpska and Brčko District, each with separate registers and rules. We trace entities and principals across all three systems and neighbouring countries, presenting ownership chains and gaps where records could not be confirmed.

05

Litigation, asset and debtor research

Creditors and litigants in Sarajevo proceedings need to locate assets and understand debtor groups. We research company holdings, property and related parties from lawful sources and locate witnesses, with any fieldwork coordinated through authorised professionals and planned with Bosnian counsel.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Sarajevo

Detective regulation in the Federation

Sarajevo city lies in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, while East Sarajevo lies in Republika Srpska, and the rules differ. The Federation's 2008 law on agencies and internal services for the protection of persons and property, with permits issued by the cantonal interior ministry, does not mention private detectives, and academic commentary indicates detective activity has lacked a statutory framework in the Federation. Any fieldwork is therefore confirmed with local counsel before it starts.

State, Federation and cantonal courts

Sarajevo is the seat of state-level judicial institutions as well as the Federation's and the canton's courts. Commercial disputes, company register matters and enforcement involving Sarajevo businesses are generally handled by the competent municipal and cantonal courts, with appeals upward through the Federation system. Counsel identifies the competent court, and investigative research is shaped to the evidence rules of that forum.

Registers across three systems

As the Bosnia and Herzegovina page explains, companies are entered in court registers kept separately in the Federation, Republika Srpska and Brčko District, and there is no operational public beneficial ownership register. For Sarajevo companies this means checking the Federation register first, then following founders and directors into the other systems, and recording what cannot be confirmed from lawful sources.

Cantonal investment and privatisation

Sarajevo Canton has its own agency for investment promotion and privatisation, which in late 2024 reported significant growth in total investment over the preceding two years. Cantonal and Federation privatisation decisions, concessions and land allocations produce public documents and disputes that are often central to due diligence on companies formerly in public ownership.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Sarajevo

TDSC has no office in Sarajevo and handles matters touching the city from Nashville. We first agree with the client and its Bosnian counsel whether the work supports an investment, a real estate or tourism project, a procurement or donor integrity question, a debt recovery or proceedings before the courts in Sarajevo, and which entity's rules apply, because the Federation and Republika Srpska regulate security and detective work differently. Research draws on court registers, procurement and privatisation records, court decisions, official gazettes and local-language media, and extends to Republika Srpska, Brčko District and neighbouring states where structures cross borders. Every matter is screened for sanctions exposure. Fieldwork is coordinated with authorised local professionals; we do not access police or official databases.

TDSC has no office in Sarajevo. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Sarajevo: Frequently Asked Questions

Are private detectives licensed in Sarajevo?

Sarajevo city is in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, whose 2008 protection agencies law covers security agencies but does not mention detectives, and commentary indicates detective work has lacked a statutory framework there. East Sarajevo is in Republika Srpska, which has its own rules. We confirm the position with Bosnian counsel for each matter before any fieldwork.

Can TDSC identify the real owners of a Sarajevo company?

We review the Federation court register for founders, directors and capital, then trace related companies across Republika Srpska, Brčko District and neighbouring countries, and add court, procurement and media sources. Because there is no operational public beneficial ownership register, we state clearly where ultimate ownership could not be confirmed from lawful sources.

Can you check a developer before we buy property in Sarajevo?

Yes. We research the developer, its landholding companies and principals for disputes, insolvency, enforcement, permit controversies and media coverage. Land and cadastral records are reviewed with local counsel, who advise on title. Findings give buyers and financiers a sourced view of counterparty and project risk before contracts are signed.

Which courts in Sarajevo hear commercial disputes?

Commercial disputes involving Sarajevo businesses are generally heard by the competent municipal and cantonal courts of the Federation, which also deal with company register and enforcement matters, with appeals upward through the Federation system. State-level courts also sit in Sarajevo for matters within their jurisdiction. Counsel identifies the right forum; we shape research to it.

Does TDSC support donor-funded or procurement integrity reviews in Sarajevo?

Yes. For donors, lenders, bidders and counsel we research contractors, subcontractors and their links to public officials using registers, procurement notices, court decisions and media. We report connections with their sources and leave conclusions about breaches to the client, its counsel and the competent authorities. We do not approach officials under pretext.
